turns.query: Use FDIC BankFind quarterly reports from 2021 Q1 through 2024 Q4. Keep the balanced bank panel with a nonmissing strictly positive reported net interest margin in every quarter, identifying banks by FDIC certificate. Use the reported annualized margin in percent. The rate regressor is the equal-fixing arithmetic mean of published New York Fed SOFR effective-date observations within each quarter, in percent. Fit a first-order dynamic individual-effects margin model with its own one-quarter lag and contemporaneous SOFR, constant slopes and no time effects. Use one-step Arellano–Bond difference GMM with homoskedastic differenced-error weighting. For the lagged dependent variable, use available level lags two through four only, collapsed by lag; there are no pre-2021 observations, and each differenced equation from 2021 Q3 onward retains its available instruments. Treat SOFR as strictly exogenous with one ordinary-IV instrument column containing its own differenced value. Include no level-equation moments or differenced intercept, and leave coefficients unrestricted. Report bank count and both coefficients. Carry the complete panel, instrument specification and fitted residuals forward, and interpret the estimated margin dynamics. Use unrounded inputs and state throughout.

Obtain the two-step heteroskedasticity-robust Arellano–Bond estimate for the carried model. Use the uncentered bank-cluster moment covariance from the preceding one-step residuals for the second-step weight, with no finite-sample multiplier or further weight update. Report both two-step coefficients and the Hansen overidentification statistic. Carry the complete two-stage estimator forward, and assess its overidentifying restrictions at the five-percent level.

For the carried two-step estimator, obtain the mean-centered delete-one-bank jackknife covariance by omitting each retained bank's complete trajectory and re-estimating both stages on the remaining fixed panel. Keep the quarterly SOFR series, model and instrument rules unchanged. Treat banks as independent clusters, and use neither bias-corrected coefficient centers nor an MSE covariance centered on the full-sample estimate. Report the standard errors of the persistence and SOFR coefficients and their sampling correlation. Carry the complete covariance and full-sample two-step coefficients forward, and assess the precision of the dynamic-rate relationship.

Use the carried full-sample two-step coefficients and complete jackknife covariance to construct the 95-percent Fieller confidence set for the model's algebraic long-run margin response to a permanent one-percentage-point SOFR increase. Use the standard-normal 97.5th percentile as the critical value and the unrestricted coefficient domain. Report the confidence-set topology and its finite boundary points in ascending order. Interpret what the set establishes about long-run sensitivity.
